collection.description: Researchers, navigators and farmers each count the seasons differently: combine their knowledge, or keep separate calendars.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject) counts the seasons by the stars, (friend) the navigator counts them by the swells and winds, and the farmers count them by the flowers. They often disagree by a week or two. (subject) wants to combine all three into one calendar, carved in a pattern like a woven basket. What should they do?

o1.name: Outcome A
o1.text: They work for a season, comparing notes every night. The calendar they carve is complicated and very beautiful, a spiral of stars, waves and flowers. It is more accurate than any of the three alone. Only four people can read it.

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: They keep their own ways. The farmers plant by the flowers, the navigators sail by the swells. When all three agree, the village knows something big is coming. That happens twice a year, and it is always right.
